title: Jeanie with the Light Brown Hair
description: A song of longing for an absent loved one, remembered through images of summer, flowing water, and a voice that is gone.
rights_note: Public domain; Stephen C. Foster died in 1864. Transcription source: Wikisource.

title: Annie Laurie
description: A declaration of lasting devotion to Annie Laurie, whose remembered promise inspires complete loyalty.
rights_note: Public domain; the modern words and tune are attributed to Alicia Scott, who died in 1900. Source index: Wikisource.

title: Believe Me If All Those Endearing Young Charms
description: A promise that love will endure after youth and beauty fade, grounded in constancy rather than appearance.
rights_note: Public domain; Thomas Moore died in 1852. Transcription source: Wikisource.

title: Beautiful Dreamer
description: A gentle serenade asking a beloved dreamer to awaken after the noise and cares of the day have passed.
rights_note: Public domain; Stephen C. Foster died in 1864. Transcription source: Wikisource.

title: Flow Gently Sweet Afton
description: A pastoral love song asking the river and nearby birds to remain quiet while the singer's beloved Mary sleeps.
rights_note: Public domain; Robert Burns died in 1796. Transcription source: Wikisource.

title: The Last Rose of Summer
description: A meditation on loneliness and mortality through the image of the final rose left after its companions have faded.
rights_note: Public domain; Thomas Moore died in 1852. Source index: Wikisource.

title: Auld Lang Syne
description: A song about preserving old friendship and shared memories despite time, distance, and separation.
rights_note: Public domain and free to use and reuse; source edition: Library of Congress, 1900.

title: Home, Sweet Home
description: A song of homesickness that values a humble home and peace of mind above travel, splendour, and palaces.
rights_note: Public domain; John Howard Payne died in 1852. Transcription source: Wikisource.
